quest.title: The Final Experiment: Withering Glory
quest.description: As the experiments proceed, Albedo obtains more and more data related to you, and the alchemy he envisages begins to take shape. Finally, after a simple test of your physical capabilities, the experiments draw to a close...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Primogem x60, Mora x27825, Guide to Ballad x5, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Head to the location of the intelligence test

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I imagine you must have encountered more than a few conundrums during your travels.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I'd like to observe your intelligence by means of a practical test of your capabilities — much as we did for the physical test.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I'd like you to explore these ruins and return with your findings.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: There are two puzzles located at the far ends of the ruins. After completion, you should be able to activate the mechanism in the center.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: As with the physical test, there are no restrictions. Everything you do is an action I wish to observe.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: A tried and tested adventurer I see.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: So, let's see you in action. Start wherever you like.

choices.text: Where there's a will, there's a way.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Remember that this is a test of intellect. So should you get lucky in any way, that won't be factored in as part of the test.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It looks like a puzzle involving Elemental Monuments.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Seelie like these are a common sight in the mountains.

talks.objective: Return to the center and activate the device
Investigate the area behind the drain

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: To the best of my knowledge, these belong to a script of some kind. They can be found all over Teyvat, but they've never given up their secrets.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: There's still a lot to learn about them, and as for why they should ever have come to rest here... A true mystery.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Let me make a copy first. I'll make time to go over them in greater detail after our research.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Another thing for the "don't understand" list. Unsolvable mystery this, weird experiment that... It'd be nice to get some cool results for once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like if you want the reward, you gotta pay the price.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I've truly gained a lot from all this. Comparatively, the little reward I can offer is too small to mention.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Let me return to the campsite first. By the time you get back, I may just have a fleeting miracle for you to witness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's kinda looking forward to seeing the result of all this brain ache...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Unless you can think of anything better to do, let's head back to the campsite.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Not so fast. You're not leaving until I'm convinced that nothing dangerous is going on here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wah! You! You didn't leave the mountain!?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I most certainly did not. And I've witnessed everything that you and Albedo have been up to.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I must say, you let your guards down. Or maybe you were drawn in by his compelling-sounding hypothesis and friendly demeanor?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Taking orders from a complete stranger, drinking anonymous potions, participating in all kinds of strange experiments?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I'd sooner believe you were tricked than that you would be so naive. Or perhaps... you were colluding from the beginning?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sister Rosaria's guard's so high, she can't even see over the top of it!

choices.text: I was just helping him with his research.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: It doesn't matter what you think, he could be a saint for all you know. But I understand him a little better than you, Outlander.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I'm only concerned with one thing: whether his alchemy has transformed you into something more sinister.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! Paimon would've sensed it. And anyway, he didn't even use any alchemy...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: With an alchemist of his level, you wouldn't sense a thing.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: In any case, I'm not about to let a potential threat back into Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what're you gonna do?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You came here to be sure, so you must have your ways of assuring yourself.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I've gotta hand it to you, you have your moments. If I can be sure that nothing you came into contact with is dangerous, that's good enough for me.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I've investigated everything else. The only items left on the agenda are these symbols.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we don't even know what they mean!

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Hmm... That much is true, not to mention... Seems like there's nothing more to them.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: But for insurance purposes, I'd better make a copy... Hmm. This is now a location of interest — regular patrols should be set up here.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Now then. All things considered, I deem that you pose no immediate threat.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Which is what I was hoping. I would have been one very unhappy Sister if you'd made me work overtime on your account.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Overtime?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Before we go our separate ways, Outlander, a word of advice. Don't be so quick to trust Albedo, and don't repeat the same mistakes that you did this time. You made a lot of rash decisions today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's gone. So stubborn!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mondstadt doesn't have many people like that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, never mind her. Let's go see Albedo!

choices.text: I don't think he's a bad person.
(I take it I passed the intelligence test.)
I feel like I've seen these before...

talks.objective: Return to the campsite and hear Albedo's conclusions

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You're back! Good timing, I've just about reached a conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You took quite a while. Did you get held up on the way back?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Time for the results. We got a myriad of data today, and it was very difficult to finish all the research in one go.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But the integral preliminary conclusion that I can offer you is... You're very much like a human from this world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You couldn't tell that just by looking?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We spent all day working our butts off for that!?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Please, I understand that this may have seemed self-evident to you, but in fact nothing in this world should be taken for granted.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Have you ever considered that the world of Teyvat may have a natural hostility to outlanders?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I mentioned the natural laws of this world. You're able to converse with me here without consequence, and nothing seems amiss. But it's arguably a small miracle.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The only other life form that, like you, has come here from afar, is the seed that I mentioned. Under the effects of Teyvat's natural laws, it isn't even able to sprout, let alone bloom.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But after I observed you, I had another idea.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Imitating you helped to inspire my alchemy, and so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! It looks like — something's appearing!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The transition from nothing into something, from shoot to stem... And now to fruition.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Is not nurturing otherworldly life also nurturing the world itself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: *sigh* It would seem that that's as far as we go. A transient bloom of incomparable beauty... Life's proudest achievement.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thought, with all our efforts, it might have bloomed forever. And it didn't even have any fruit...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Life is a manifold tapestry of free entities, its value shouldn't derive from how long it stays with us. Even a momentary burst is precious.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: A short life can be well-lived. A life lived efficiently, lived to perfection, is necessarily one unburdened by loneliness.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: So, do you understand what I meant about us conversing here arguably being a small miracle?

choices.text: Well, I haven't withered just yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Things feel a little heavy right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hehehe, don't be sad, {NICKNAME}, you've got Paimon to look after you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Albedo, Paimon really wants to be your friend.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: ...Thank you both. Even if dispelling loneliness is not essential for life, it certainly doesn't hurt.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #Your help inspired me to discover the means to make a flower bloom, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So I'm a helpful specimen?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I mean that the time that I've spent traveling with you in the mountains was a valuable journey for me.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In the future... If the need arises... Can I solicit your help again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure, even if you just want some company, find me anytime.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Well... Glad I can count on you.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #I made a point throughout of telling {M#him}{F#her} how ordinary the results were...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But what was that sediment I saw forming at the bottom of the vial? It should not have been there... What could it mean?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Those born of earth are bound by its imperfections, but those born of chalk are free of impurities... You and I are alike, both composed of a substance that has yet to be fully defined...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If one day, I lose control... destroy Mondstadt... destroy everything...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Can I rely on you to stop me?

choices.text: Quite literally, by a sister no less.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Aha, I wouldn't worry, she's just doing her job.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh? Seems that the water level has suddenly decreased.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We should be able to see what's in the water now, let's have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Returning them to their rightful places is up to you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Sorry, there's been a lot of issues with the research, many of the inferences I collated just don't tally with the data from the experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: On the other hand, some of the conclusions that Albedo derived from his own intuition have been borne out by the facts.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: I'm just glad that we've seen some progress, so uh... No reason to be dejected! Albedo said I did a good job!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: If you want to hear the results in detail, you'd be better talking to him. I've got work to do.
